src/auth.mts.reason: Locked-auth transactions set their lock_timeout (set_config), withLockedAuthByEmail and signInOidcUser take the team controller's email advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock), and the start-up checks read pg_attribute for the tables and columns and pg_index for the unique indexes on lower(email) and on account (providerId, accountId); Drizzle has no builder for any of them. revokeProviderSessions deletes verification rows (the provider's challenges, then the known devices of the users it signed out), which have no Drizzle table in the common schema. The user-row locks, the credential read, the identity rows and the session deletes are typed Drizzle queries.

src/check.mts.reason: Not statements: the raw-statement scanner's own comments and patterns name the forms it counts.

src/db.mts.reason: transaction() sends BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK on its checked-out connection so it can release or discard it; Drizzle has no builder for transaction control.

src/migration-ledger.mts.reason: The migration ledger applies migration files as SQL text and takes its advisory locks and schema_version rows on a pg client before any app schema exists.

src/tenancy-testing.mts.reason: Test-only: sets the scope on a pg connection the test owns; Drizzle has no builder for set_config.

src/tenancy.mts.reason: The policy expression is DDL, which takes no bind parameters; set_config and current_setting have no Drizzle builder; the boot role check reads system catalogues on a pg pool.

src/workspace-team.mts.reason: The team controller predates the Drizzle team tables and takes a plain pg client (TeamClient); part two of the framework moves it to typed Drizzle queries and lowers this entry. acceptVerifiedOidcInvitation's identity row (#143) is one of them, in the same transaction as the account it links.
